Unaccompanied Baggage: Unaccompanied baggage refers to any baggage that is not brought by the passenger themselves.
Baggage: Baggage is defined as reasonable quantities of food, apparel, household items, or other personal effects imported by a passenger for personal use. Each individual item categorized as baggage must not exceed a specific weight threshold.
Passenger: The term passenger refers specifically to any non-tourist arriving from abroad.
Gold Ornament: Gold ornaments are defined as wearable jewelry made of gold that is twenty-two karat or less in purity.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers arriving by air or sea aged twelve years or older are entitled to import a specific weight of baggage duty-free. Additionally, they may import a further specified weight of clothing, personal effects, and study materials free of all duties and taxes.
Passengers under the age of twelve are limited to a smaller duty-free baggage allowance, and they are not eligible for other specific duty-free concessions granted to adult passengers.
Professional Equipment: Passengers are permitted to import portable equipment used for their professional duties without payment of customs duties and taxes.
Gold and Silver: Passengers may import gold or silver jewelry, bars, or ingots up to specified weight limits upon payment of applicable duties and taxes, provided that declared amounts exceeding these limits are subject to forfeiture.
A limited amount of gold or silver jewelry can be imported duty-free by passengers, subject to quantity restrictions on the number of individual pieces.
Alcoholic Beverages: Foreign passport holders are permitted to import a limited volume of alcoholic beverages duty-free. Bangladeshi passport holders are strictly prohibited from importing any alcoholic beverages.
Electronic Appliances: The regulations define specific duty-free and dutiable items that passengers may import, including household electronics, computers, and mobile phones, subject to quantity and value thresholds. Specific appliances are listed in statutory schedules with corresponding fixed duty rates payable by the passenger.
Unaccompanied Baggage: Unaccompanied baggage must be declared using the prescribed form and cleared according to customs policies. If the baggage arrives separately from the passenger, it is treated as if it were imported personally by the passenger.

Airline Crew: Bangladeshi crew or staff members of Bangladeshi or foreign airlines arriving from abroad during official duty are permitted to import baggage up to a specified monetary limit free of all duties and taxes.
Seafarers: Bangladeshi crew or staff arriving from foreign seaports are permitted to import baggage up to a specified monetary limit free of all duties and taxes.
